thesis: Strategy v1 (2026-11-11). HOLD $1,000 cash in the separate spot crypto paper portfolio; reassess at the next completed UTC Coinbase daily bar, and daily thereafter. Verified GitHub state/agent context as of 2026-11-18 21:45 UTC: $1,000 cash, no holdings, no pending orders, all prior crypto decisions processed as HOLD, no fills. The latest completed 2026-11-17 Coinbase BTC-USD bar closed $64,873.18; its 20-day average was $73,443.897 (falling from $77,219.8865 five days earlier), and five-day return was -9.102885%. BTC closed ~11.67% below the declining average. This completed bar is NOT a November 18 executable quote. On common November 17 marks the cash portfolio is $1,000 versus $853.942118 for the passive BTC benchmark, an advantage from cash exposure during a drawdown, not proof of signal skill. November 18 CoinDesk reporting describes BTC around $64,100 in its morning snapshot, weak risk appetite, and reduced basis-trade yields; a Reuters November 18 report details the fallout of a large Binance security breach. Reports of ETF outflows and macro causation are provisional secondary claims, not verified on-chain measurements. ETH ($1,822.15), SOL ($75.11), ADA ($0.15515) and LINK ($9.311) have November 17 completed Coinbase USD closes, but none has a sufficiently differentiated verified catalyst to justify replacing the BTC-versus-cash framework. A modest BTC position can be justified on broad exposure grounds, but the falling average, negative five-day return, security uncertainty and trading costs make cash more defensible today. Reconsider a roughly 5–15% BTC paper entry after a completed close above the 20-day average with improving five-day return, or a multi-day stabilization and independently corroborated improvement in market conditions; do not require a guaranteed forecast. No strategy revision warranted. November is still partial; the context reports no prior October month for review.
